balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Autodesk, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Autodesk, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Autodesk, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Autodesk, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Autodesk, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Autodesk, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Autodesk, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Autodesk, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Autodesk, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Autodesk, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

subscription.title: Subscription mix
subscription.content:
Subscription revenue is recurring; services revenue (implementation, training) is lower-margin and lumpy.

For Autodesk, Inc.: a rising subscription share improves gross margin and predictability.

What to watch:

  • Subscription as a share of total revenue

rpo.title: Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO)
rpo.content:
RPO is contracted subscription revenue not yet recognised -- Autodesk's own forward-demand KPI, disclosed every quarter since the move to term-only licensing. Current RPO is the slice due to convert to revenue within 12 months.

For Autodesk, Inc.: RPO growth leads reported revenue growth because it captures signed multi-year commitments before they are billed or recognised -- it is the best read on demand before it shows up in the P&L.

What to watch:

  • Current RPO growth versus total RPO growth (shortening duration is a flag)
  • RPO growth decelerating faster than revenue growth (a leading indicator, not a lagging one)

recurringRevenue.title: Recurring revenue mix
recurringRevenue.content:
Recurring revenue (subscription plus maintenance on legacy perpetual licences) as a % of total revenue tracks how far Autodesk's 2016 shift away from perpetual licences has run. Maintenance revenue is the shrinking legacy piece -- support on licences sold before the subscription transition.

For Autodesk, Inc.: the model is essentially fully transitioned when maintenance approaches zero and recurring % approaches 100; what is left to watch is net new recurring revenue, not the mix shift itself.

What to watch:

  • Recurring % closing in on 100% (little further margin lift left from mix)
  • Maintenance revenue run-off rate

productMix.title: Revenue by product line
productMix.content:
Revenue split by end-market product family: AEC (architecture, engineering & construction), AutoCAD (and AutoCAD LT), Manufacturing, Media & Entertainment, Make (Fusion-based manufacturing operations, Autodesk's newest reportable growth line) and Other products.

For Autodesk, Inc.: AEC and Manufacturing are management's stated growth priorities (construction digitisation, factory automation); AutoCAD is the mature base that funds them.

What to watch:

  • AEC and Manufacturing growing faster than AutoCAD (mix shift to the stated priorities)
  • Make's growth rate versus the rest of the manufacturing portfolio

geography.title: Revenue by region
geography.content:
Revenue split between the Americas, EMEA and APAC regions, each billed and recognised in local currency then translated to USD.

For Autodesk, Inc.: roughly half of revenue is non-US, so a strengthening dollar is a reported-growth headwind even when local demand is steady -- check this chart against currency commentary in the MD&A before reading a growth deceleration as organic.

What to watch:

  • EMEA/APAC growth diverging from Americas (regional demand, not just FX)
  • Constant-currency growth disclosed in the filing versus the as-reported numbers here
